title: Define execution model (sync vs async job system)
description: Decide and specify how the product layer invokes the engine: synchronous request/response vs asynchronous job (job_id + status polling/callback). Engine pipeline is long-running, so this drives the background-jobs design (.18). Output the chosen request/response/envelope shapes and status lifecycle.
design:
# Decision: Engine Execution Model — Async Job System (.21.2)

> Task: `variation-audit-z3x.21.2` · Parent: `.21` (engine integration) · Relates: blocks `.18` (background jobs)
> Status: **accepted** (2026-06-27, founder-approved with defaults) · Contract: extends [engine-product-api-contract-v1](../engine-product-api-contract-v1.md)
>
> **MVP settings (locked):** polling-only (no webhook) · 15-min job timeout · no cancellation.

## 1. Decision
Adopt an **asynchronous, job-based execution model** as the primary (and for MVP, the only required) way the product layer invokes the engine.

**Why not synchronous:** the engine runs a multi-stage LLM pipeline (ingest → baseline → classify → quantify → confidence) over many documents using `claude-opus-4-8` with adaptive thinking. Per-project runtime is seconds-to-minutes and grows with document count — well beyond a safe HTTP/proxy timeout (30–60s). A synchronous call would time out, hold connections, and give no progress feedback.

**Optional later:** a thin synchronous `POST /v1/quick-check` for a *single* document (<~10s, no cross-document evidence linking) for interactive "is this a variation?" UX. **Not in MVP scope** — listed under Future.

## 2. API Surface

### Create a job
```
POST /v1/analyses
```
Body = Input Schema v1, plus the `.21.4` envelope fields (`request_id`, `contract_version`) and an optional `callback_url`.

Response — `202 Accepted`:
```json
{
  "job_id": "string",
  "status": "queued",
  "request_id": "string",
  "created_at": "ISO8601",
  "links": { "self": "/v1/analyses/{job_id}" }
}
```

### Poll a job
```
GET /v1/analyses/{job_id}
```
Response — `200 OK`:
```json
{
  "job_id": "string",
  "project_id": "string",
  "status": "queued | running | succeeded | failed | canceled",
  "progress": { "stage": "classify", "percent": 0.6 },
  "result": { "...Output Schema v1, present only when status=succeeded..." },
  "error": { "code": "string", "message": "string", "retryable": false },
  "engine_version": "v1",
  "created_at": "ISO8601",
  "updated_at": "ISO8601"
}
```

### Cancel a job — POST-MVP (not implemented for MVP)
```
DELETE /v1/analyses/{job_id}   ->   status: canceled (if not terminal)
```
> Deferred per §10. MVP has no cancellation and no `canceled` state.

### Callback (optional)
If `callback_url` is supplied, the engine `POST`s the full poll payload to it once on reaching a **terminal** state (`succeeded|failed|canceled`). Polling remains the source of truth; the webhook is an optimization. Callbacks are signed (HMAC header) and retried with backoff.

## 3. Status Lifecycle (MVP)
```
queued ──► running ──► succeeded
               │
               └─────► failed      (terminal, may be retryable; incl. 15-min ENGINE_TIMEOUT)
```
- `queued` — accepted, awaiting a worker.
- `running` — a worker is executing the pipeline; `progress.stage` reflects the current engine stage.
- Terminal states (`succeeded`, `failed`) never transition further. A failed+retryable job is re-run by **submitting a new job** (same `request_id` is rejected as duplicate — see idempotency), not by mutating the old one.
- No `canceled` state in MVP (cancellation deferred — see §10).

## 4. Result Delivery
- MVP: result returned **inline** in the poll payload when `status=succeeded`.
- Guardrail: if the serialized result exceeds a size cap (e.g. 1 MB), return `result_url` to a stored artifact instead of inline `result`. (Defer artifact storage until a project actually exceeds the cap.)

## 5. Idempotency, Tracing, Retries  (interlocks with .21.4)
- `request_id` is the **idempotency key**: a repeat `POST` with the same `request_id` returns the *existing* job (`200`, not a new `202`) within a dedup window (e.g. 7 days). Prevents duplicate-charge double-runs.
- `request_id` is echoed on every response and logged across product + engine for tracing.
- **Internal** retries: transient LLM/API errors (429/5xx) are retried inside the worker with exponential backoff; only exhausted transients surface as `failed` with `retryable=true`.
- Clients must **not** auto-resubmit on timeout — they poll; the job is still running.

## 6. Error Envelope
```json
{ "error": { "code": "INVALID_INPUT | ENGINE_TIMEOUT | LLM_UNAVAILABLE | INTERNAL",
             "message": "human readable",
             "retryable": true,
             "details": { } } }
```
Validation failures are caught **synchronously at POST** (`400`, no job created). Processing failures appear on the job as `status=failed`.

## 7. SLAs / Client Guidance
- POST→`202` ack: < 1s (just enqueues).
- Poll cadence: client uses backoff — start 2s, cap 15s. (Or rely on `callback_url`.)
- Soft per-job processing timeout (configurable; e.g. 15 min) → `failed/ENGINE_TIMEOUT`.

## 8. Mapping to .18 (Background Jobs)
This decision **defines the contract** that `.18` implements:
- A durable job queue + a `jobs` table (`job_id`, `request_id`, `status`, `progress`, `result_ref`, `error`, timestamps).
- A worker pool that consumes the queue, runs the reused engine pipeline, writes status transitions, then fires notifications + the optional webhook.
- Queue tech is an `.18`/architecture (`.1`) choice (DB-backed queue is simplest for MVP; Redis/RQ or Celery if scale demands). **Not decided here.**

## 9. Future Extensions
- `POST /v1/quick-check` synchronous single-doc preview.
- Streaming progress via SSE/WebSocket (supersedes polling for live UX).
- Incremental / delta analysis (re-run only new documents) — pairs with contract §7.
- Multi-project batch submission.

## 10. Resolved Decisions (2026-06-27, founder-approved)
1. **Webhook:** ❌ not in MVP — **polling-only**. `callback_url` and the webhook flow move to Future (§9). The product layer polls `GET /v1/analyses/{job_id}` with backoff.
2. **Max processing time:** **15 minutes**, then the job is force-failed with `status=failed`, `error.code=ENGINE_TIMEOUT`, `retryable=true`.
3. **Cancellation:** ❌ not in MVP — drop `DELETE /v1/analyses/{job_id}`. Lifecycle is `queued → running → succeeded | failed` only (no `canceled` state for MVP). Revisit post-MVP.
notes: Proposed: async job-based model (POST /v1/analyses -> 202 job_id; GET poll; optional webhook). Spec at docs/decisions/21.2-execution-model.md. Awaiting founder confirm on 3 open questions.

title: ADR: Hybrid architecture - reuse engine + new product layer + Beads orchestration
description: DECISION (2026-06-27): Hybrid architecture. REUSE the existing AI detection engine from the prior changeorder-recovery project (proven on synthetic data: ingest/baseline/classify/quantify/confidence pipeline). BUILD a new product layer on top (auth, orgs, project upload, multi-source ingestion, commercial review workflow, reporting, dashboard). Use Beads for workflow tracking and orchestration. Rationale: avoid rebuilding a validated engine; focus new effort on product/UX, ingestion, and review/reporting. Implication: tasks .9-.13 are ADAPT/INTEGRATE work, not greenfield; new task .21 owns the port + engine/product API contract.

title: Integrate existing detection engine (reuse from changeorder-recovery)
description: Port/wrap the existing AI detection engine from the changeorder-recovery repo (backend/app/ai: ingest -> baseline -> classify -> quantify -> confidence; FastAPI + SQLAlchemy, model claude-opus-4-8) as a reusable engine service/module, and define a stable API contract between the engine and the new Beads-orchestrated product layer. Engine is REUSED, not rebuilt.

# Engine ↔ Product API Contract (v1)

> Owner task: `variation-audit-z3x.21` (Integrate existing detection engine).
> Status: v1 draft. Engine reused from `changeorder-recovery`; product layer built on top (Beads-orchestrated).

## 1. Core Principle
The AI engine (from changeorder-recovery) is treated as a black-box service.
The Beads product layer does NOT modify internal logic — it only sends structured inputs and receives structured outputs.

---

## 2. Input Schema (Product → Engine)

All requests sent to the engine must follow this structure:

```json
{
  "project_id": "string",
  "company_id": "string",
  "project_type": "construction_trade",
  "country": "AU",
  "documents": [
    {
      "type": "email | rfi | site_instruction | meeting_note | sms | document",
      "timestamp": "ISO8601",
      "source": "string (email thread / file / system)",
      "content": "raw text"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 3. Engine Processing Responsibilities

The engine must:
- Parse unstructured construction communication
- Detect potential variation events
- Link evidence across multiple documents
- Assign confidence score per variation
- Estimate commercial impact (optional stage)

---

## 4. Output Schema (Engine → Product)

```json
{
  "project_id": "string",
  "variations": [
    {
      "variation_id": "string",
      "title": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "status": "detected | confirmed | uncertain",
      "confidence_score": 0.0,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "type": "email | rfi | instruction | note",
          "reference": "string",
          "quote": "string excerpt"
        }
      ],
      "estimated_value": {
        "amount": 0,
        "currency": "AUD",
        "confidence": "low | medium | high"
      }
    }
  ],
  "engine_version": "v1"
}
```

> `confidence_score` is a float in the range 0.0–1.0.

---

## 5. Boundaries

Engine is NOT responsible for:
- UI rendering
- user authentication
- project management
- workflow orchestration
- notifications

Product layer is NOT responsible for:
- AI inference logic
- variation detection rules
- scoring algorithms

---

## 6. Versioning Rule

All outputs must include:

```json
"engine_version": "v1"
```

---

## 7. Future Extensions

- streaming mode (real-time ingestion)
- incremental updates (delta analysis)
- multi-project batching

title: Variation detection engine
description: Analyze normalized data to identify legitimate unclaimed variations (scope changes not captured in the original contract value).
notes: REUSE: adapt the classify stage of the existing engine for variation detection.

title: AI document parsing & normalization
description: Parse all ingested sources with AI into a normalized internal schema (entities, dates, references, scope items) for downstream engines.
notes: REUSE: adapt from changeorder-recovery backend/app/ai (ingest + baseline stages) for parsing/normalization.

title: Architecture & system design
description: Define the overall system architecture: services, data model, storage, AI pipeline, and tech stack. Produce diagrams and an MVP technical plan.

title: Add request_id + contract_version for tracing & idempotency
description: Add request_id (idempotency + tracing) and contract_version to the input envelope, complementing output engine_version. Define idempotency semantics and how versions are negotiated/validated.

title: Standardize confidence system (score vs categorical)
description: Define the relationship between per-variation confidence_score (0.0-1.0 float) and estimated_value.confidence (low|medium|high). Specify mapping/threshold rules so the product layer renders confidence consistently everywhere.

title: Project creation & completed-project upload

title: Set up variation-audit workflow
description:
Set up the initial workflow for the Variation Audit project.

The goal is to establish the project structure, define the development roadmap, identify the core modules, and prepare the AI agent workflow using Beads.

The MVP should help construction contractors analyze completed projects, identify legitimate unclaimed variations from project evidence (emails, RFIs, site instructions, meeting minutes, and other documents), collect supporting evidence, estimate potential recoverable value, and generate a review report for the commercial team.

This task should result in a clear architecture, prioritized backlog, and implementation plan for the MVP.

title: Notifications & background jobs
description: Async job queue for ingestion/AI processing plus user notifications on completion and review events.

title: Audit trail & evidence viewer
description: Immutable audit trail of actions and a viewer to inspect each variation's source evidence in context.

title: Dashboard & project UI
description: Project dashboard showing variations, status, totals, and entry points into review and reports.

title: SMS / document ingestion
description: Ingest SMS exports and generic documents (PDF, DOCX, images) as additional evidence sources.

title: Meeting minutes ingestion
description: Ingest meeting minutes, extracting decisions and action items relevant to scope changes.

title: Site instructions ingestion
description: Ingest site instructions / architect/engineer instructions issued during the project.

title: RFI ingestion
description: Ingest Requests for Information (RFIs) and responses, preserving references and timestamps.
